page.layout: One printed page, single column. Title block centred at top; verse poem in the middle with a woodcut initial O; dedication line, signature lines and a catchword-like "In" at the foot. No margin notes. Digitiser watermark at lower right is omitted.

main_text.head: Ad Historiam
D. PIERII WINSEMII, IC. Eloquentiae & Historiarum dum viveret, Professoris & Historiographi Illustr. Frisiae Ordinum Celeberrimi.
main_text.p: OS magnum, quod magna Dei miracula narrat, Quae nostros tantum cernere fecit avos, Dum vox imbellis populi & suspiria mixta Sanguine ruperunt vincula dura Erebi, Regnaque quaßarunt, & celso culmine structum Mundique æquatum finibus imperium, Pondere sub cuius, nutantis vulnere vasto, Iam pridem rerum machina tota gemit: Dum tener astuti rejecit frena PHILIPPI Belga vovens soli libera corda Deo. Qualia non Tacitus non aurea vena Maronis Explicuit sive bis doctius ingenium. Os felix, cui tanta datum est nudare nepoti Risuro fumos labilis imperij, WINSEMII; quod nec voluit mors dura silère. Verba etenim seclis pagina tradet anus:
Honori Collegae dum vivebat amandi & observandi, post obitum desiderati, raptim ponebat.
IOHANNES COCCEIUS Doct. S. Theol. & Ling. Hebraea Professor, ac pro tempore Rector in Acad. Franekerana.

page.notes: The initial O is a large woodcut letter. Several lines of the verse are set in italic; the first letter of the poem is the woodcut initial. The word "In" at the foot is a catchword-like fragment starting the next section. Some words are doubtful due to scan quality, notably "Qualia" and "Risuro", which are transcribed as printed.
